newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat goes to Europe, will probably go to summit.
newsitem.headline: Arafat goes to Europe, will probably go to summit.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat left for Luxembourg on Monday after a day of inconclusive discussions on whether he and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak should go to a Middle East summit in Washington.

"He (Arafat) will probably go," said Egyptian presidential adviser Osama el-Baz, who took part in the consultations between Arafat and Mubarak near the Mediterranean city of Alexandria. He said the summit would take place in Washington on Wednesday.

A Palestinian official said earlier Arafat would go first to Luxembourg to see European foreign ministers and then to Washington. Arafat and more senior PLO people would not confirm he had taken a final decision on the summit.
The Palestinian ambassador to Cairo, Zuhdi el-Kudra, told reporters at Cairo airport: "It hasn't been decided yet." Asked when Arafat would decide, he said: "Tonight."
Arafat himself said only: "I have now a meeting with the Troika (of European Union foreign ministers in Luxembourg) and I am going to meet the Troika."
Baz said Egypt would have to decide very shortly if Mubarak would go to the summit, called by President Bill Clinton in response to violence between Israelis and Palestinians.
"The important thing is that the summit is taking place with the parties immediately involved in the conflict," he added.
Arafat and Mubarak seemed earlier on Monday to be in revolt against U.S. diplomacy, refusing to rush into a meeting with Netanyahu until they know what Israel might offer.

"Mubarak wants to see a clearly defined programme of action (by Israel). And he doesn't want to get involved in an unsuccessful summit," said an Arab diplomat close to Monday's talks between Arafat and Mubarak.
"So far the Israelis are still being intransigent. Contacts are continuing but the position is not clear," he added.
Clinton called for the summit to help end five days of clashes in which 55 Palestinians and 14 Israelis have died.
Baz denied earlier reports by Palestinian officials that Arafat had asked for a postponement of the summit but said the leaders would meet on Wednesday instead of Tuesday, after preparatory meetings.

Asked if Egypt was setting any conditions for attending the meeting, he said: "No, usually we don't attach any conditions to our position because we don't like to present anybody with ultimatums or conditions.

"Our only concern is how best to serve the cause of peace, to produce tangible and concrete results on the ground and revive the hope in the minds and hearts of the people in the region that the peace process is still alive."
He denied Egypot was upset that Clinton overtook Egypt's plans to bring Arafat and Netanyahu together in Cairo.
"The venue of the conference is not the important thing. The important thing is the content and the result. What would the summit produce -- this is the important thing," he said.
